requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: The header consists of six 16-bit words, totaling 96 bits (12 octets).
requirements.why_checkable: The diagram gives six complete 16-bit rows, allowing the total header length to be checked.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the ID field in the first 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The ID bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the QR field in bit 0 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The QR bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the OPCODE field in bits 1 through 4 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The OPCODE bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the AA field in bit 5 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The AA bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the TC field in bit 6 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The TC bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the RD field in bit 7 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The RD bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the RA field in bit 8 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.
requirements.why_checkable: The RA bit offset and encoded width can be checked against header bytes.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Z field in bits 9 through 11 of the second 16-bit word, occupying exactly that slot.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a DNS message header

requirements.quote:
ID              A 16 bit identifier assigned by the program that
                generates any kind of query.  This identifier is copied
requirements.condition: When generating any kind of query
requirements.required_behavior: Have the program that generates the query assign its ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The outgoing query ID assignment can be inspected at query generation.

requirements.quote:
ID              A 16 bit identifier assigned by the program that
                generates any kind of query.  This identifier is copied
                the corresponding reply and can be used by the requester
                to match up replies to outstanding queries.
requirements.condition: When generating the reply corresponding to a query
requirements.required_behavior: Copy the query ID into the corresponding reply.
requirements.why_checkable: The query and reply IDs can be compared for equality.

requirements.quote:
ID              A 16 bit identifier assigned by the program that
                generates any kind of query.  This identifier is copied
                the corresponding reply and can be used by the requester
                to match up replies to outstanding queries.
requirements.condition: When a requester elects to use the ID to correlate replies with outstanding queries
requirements.required_behavior: The requester may use the copied ID to match a reply to an outstanding query; this use is permitted, not required.
requirements.why_checkable: A requester using this permitted correlation method can be checked against outstanding query IDs.

requirements.quote:
QR              A one bit field that specifies whether this message is a
                query (0), or a response (1).
requirements.condition: When encoding a query message
requirements.required_behavior: Set QR to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The query header QR bit has a fixed value.

requirements.quote:
QR              A one bit field that specifies whether this message is a
                query (0), or a response (1).
requirements.condition: When encoding a response message
requirements.required_behavior: Set QR to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The response header QR bit has a fixed value.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:
requirements.condition: When originating a query
requirements.required_behavior: Set OPCODE to specify the kind of query being originated.
requirements.why_checkable: The originating query operation and outgoing OPCODE can be compared.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:
requirements.condition: When generating the response to a query
requirements.required_behavior: Copy OPCODE from the query into the response.
requirements.why_checkable: A query and its response must have equal OPCODE fields.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:

                0               a standard query (QUERY)
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting OPCODE for a standard query (QUERY)
requirements.required_behavior: Use OPCODE value 0 for a standard query (QUERY).
requirements.why_checkable: The standard query (QUERY) operation has an explicit numeric OPCODE encoding.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:

                0               a standard query (QUERY)

                1               an inverse query (IQUERY)
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting OPCODE for a inverse query (IQUERY)
requirements.required_behavior: Use OPCODE value 1 for a inverse query (IQUERY).
requirements.why_checkable: The inverse query (IQUERY) operation has an explicit numeric OPCODE encoding.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:

                0               a standard query (QUERY)

                1               an inverse query (IQUERY)

                2               a server status request (STATUS)
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting OPCODE for a server status request (STATUS)
requirements.required_behavior: Use OPCODE value 2 for a server status request (STATUS).
requirements.why_checkable: The server status request (STATUS) operation has an explicit numeric OPCODE encoding.

requirements.quote:
OPCODE          A four bit field that specifies kind of query in this
                message.  This value is set by the originator of a query
                and copied into the response.  The values are:

                0               a standard query (QUERY)

                1               an inverse query (IQUERY)

                2               a server status request (STATUS)

requirements.condition: When interpreting OPCODE according to this header format
requirements.required_behavior: Treat OPCODE values 3 through 15 as reserved for future use.
requirements.why_checkable: The opcode table distinguishes reserved values from the three defined query kinds.

requirements.quote:
AA              Authoritative Answer - this bit is valid in responses,
                and specifies that the responding name server is an
                authority for the domain name in question section.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the AA flag
requirements.required_behavior: Apply its Authoritative Answer meaning to responses.
requirements.why_checkable: The message type determines whether AA carries the defined response semantics.

requirements.quote:
AA              Authoritative Answer - this bit is valid in responses,
                and specifies that the responding name server is an
                authority for the domain name in question section.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a response with AA set
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret AA as indicating that the responding name server is an authority for the domain name in the question section.
requirements.why_checkable: The AA assertion can be compared with the responding server's authority for the question name.

requirements.quote:
AA              Authoritative Answer - this bit is valid in responses,
                and specifies that the responding name server is an
                authority for the domain name in question section.

                multiple owner names because of aliases.  The AA bit

requirements.quote:
TC              TrunCation - specifies that this message was truncated
                due to length greater than that permitted on the
                transmission channel.
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting TC
requirements.required_behavior: Use TC to indicate that the message was truncated because its length exceeded the length permitted on its transmission channel.
requirements.why_checkable: The TC indication can be checked against whether channel-length truncation occurred.

requirements.quote:
RD              Recursion Desired - this bit may be set in a query and
                is copied into the response.  If RD is set, it directs
                the name server to pursue the query recursively.
                Recursive query support is optional.
requirements.condition: When generating a query
requirements.required_behavior: The query originator may set RD to request recursion.
requirements.why_checkable: A query with RD set is an explicitly permitted encoding of a recursion request.

requirements.quote:
RD              Recursion Desired - this bit may be set in a query and
                is copied into the response.  If RD is set, it directs
                the name server to pursue the query recursively.
                Recursive query support is optional.
requirements.condition: When generating a response to a query
requirements.required_behavior: Copy the RD bit from the query into the response.
requirements.why_checkable: The RD bits can be compared across a query and its corresponding response.

requirements.quote:
RD              Recursion Desired - this bit may be set in a query and
                is copied into the response.  If RD is set, it directs
                the name server to pursue the query recursively.
                Recursive query support is optional.
requirements.condition: When RD is set in a query and the name server provides the optional recursive-query support
requirements.required_behavior: Pursue the query recursively.
requirements.why_checkable: The RD-set request can be checked for entry into recursive processing on a server that supports recursion.

requirements.quote:
RD              Recursion Desired - this bit may be set in a query and
                is copied into the response.  If RD is set, it directs
                the name server to pursue the query recursively.
                Recursive query support is optional.
requirements.condition: When selecting whether a name server implements recursive-query support
requirements.required_behavior: Recursive-query support is optional.
requirements.why_checkable: A server lacking recursive-query support is explicitly permitted by this capability requirement.

requirements.quote:
RA              Recursion Available - this be is set or cleared in a
                response, and denotes whether recursive query support is
                available in the name server.
requirements.condition: When generating a response and recursive-query support is available in the name server
requirements.required_behavior: Set RA to indicate that recursive-query support is available.
requirements.why_checkable: The response RA bit can be compared with the server's availability of recursive-query support.

requirements.quote:
RA              Recursion Available - this be is set or cleared in a
                response, and denotes whether recursive query support is
                available in the name server.
requirements.condition: When generating a response and recursive-query support is unavailable in the name server
requirements.required_behavior: Clear RA to indicate that recursive-query support is unavailable.
requirements.why_checkable: The response RA bit can be compared with the absence of recursive-query support.

requirements.quote:
Z               Reserved for future use.  Must be zero in all queries
                and responses.
requirements.condition: In every query and response
requirements.required_behavior: Set the reserved Z field to zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The entire reserved Z field has a fixed zero value in either message type.

requirements.quote:

                responses.  The values have the following
                interpretation:
requirements.condition: When generating a response
requirements.required_behavior: Set the RCODE field as part of the response.
requirements.why_checkable: A response header can be inspected for its response-code assignment.

requirements.quote:
RCODE           Response code - this 4 bit field is set as part of
                responses.  The values have the following
                interpretation:

                0               No error condition
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting a response with no error condition
requirements.required_behavior: Use RCODE 0 to represent no error condition.
requirements.why_checkable: The no-error result has an explicitly defined numeric response code.

requirements.quote:
RCODE           Response code - this 4 bit field is set as part of
                responses.  The values have the following
                interpretation:

                0               No error condition

                1               Format error - The name server was
                                unable to interpret the query.
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting a format-error response indicating that the name server was unable to interpret the query
requirements.required_behavior: Use RCODE 1 for this format error.
requirements.error_behavior: Represent the query-interpretation failure with RCODE 1 in a format-error response.
requirements.why_checkable: The format-error response code can be checked directly.

requirements.quote:
RCODE           Response code - this 4 bit field is set as part of
                responses.  The values have the following
                interpretation:

                0               No error condition

                1               Format error - The name server was
                                unable to interpret the query.

                2               Server failure - The name server was
                                unable to process this query due to a
                                problem with the name server.
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting a server-failure response indicating that a problem with the name server prevented it from processing the query
requirements.required_behavior: Use RCODE 2 for this server failure.
requirements.error_behavior: Represent the server-side processing failure with RCODE 2 in a server-failure response.
requirements.why_checkable: The server-failure response code can be checked directly.
